title: Case L — 9 x 14 cube array, line source, non-isothermal
summary: 14 rows by 9 columns of 0.06 m cubes with a tracer line source on the floor across the tunnel, in an unstably stratified boundary layer: velocity, temperature, concentration and their fluxes at 344 points in the streets and over the roofs.

configuration.array: 14 rows (along x) by 9 columns (across y) of cubes, H = 0.06 m, pitch 0.12 m (street width = H, plan area ratio 25 %), published as BD_caseL.stl; the data paper calls it '9 rows by 14 columns'
measurement_planes: 8 heights (4 .. 150 mm) at 27 locations in the streets near the source
4 heights (70 .. 150 mm) at 14 locations above the blocks
configuration.stratification: unstable: floor 45.0 degC, air at z = H 14.75 degC (difference 30.3 K), bulk Richardson number -0.035 (workbook; the readme says -0.04); the workbook gives the building surface as 42.2 degC
configuration.source: floor line source across the tunnel at x = -0.15 m between rows 7 and 8: readme 0.037 m x 1.2 m, BD_caseL.stl patch 0.04 m x 1.02 m; 100 % ethylene, 8.33e-6 m3/s (500 cc/min) at 35 degC
configuration.concentration_normalisation: c0 = q / (U_H H^2) = 1728.23 ppm (the workbook's value)
configuration.instrument: split-fibre hot wire (velocity), cold wire (temperature), high-speed hydrocarbon analyser (concentration), 1000 Hz with a 200 Hz low-pass filter, 60 s per point
configuration.tunnel: thermally stratified wind tunnel, Tokyo Polytechnic University (Atsugi); 1.2 m wide, 1.0 m high; 26 aluminium angles 9 mm high every 200 mm as roughness; model floor 10 mm above the tunnel floor
configuration.scale_note: model scale; the sources state no model:full scale ratio

units.temperature: degC (T); K (T_rms); heat fluxes K m/s; concentration fluxes ppm m/s

frame.origin: bottom centre of the windward wall of the 9th row (of 14) of the central column: x = 0 is that wall, y = 0 the centre line of the central column
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x); row k spans x in [0.12 (k-9), 0.12 (k-9) + 0.06], so the array spans x in [-0.96, 0.66]
frame.y: +y lateral; column centres at y = 0, +-0.12, ... +-0.48 (the array spans y in [-0.51, 0.51])
frame.z: +z up from the model floor; cube tops at z = 0.06; heated floor at z = 0

inflow_fit.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.32 m (about 5 H) on the workbook's Inflow sheet (CSV = its rounding)
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; the boundary layer is unstably stratified, so a neutral log law is only a rough description

fit.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.32 m (about 5 H) on the workbook's Inflow sheet (CSV = its rounding)
fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; the boundary layer is unstably stratified, so a neutral log law is only a rough description

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): a log-law inlet fitted to the case's own approach-flow file, with k and epsilon from the standard neutral ABL relations. Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) = u*/kappa ln((z + z0)/z0); k = u*^2 / sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))
recommended.fit: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.32 m (about 5 H) on the workbook's Inflow sheet (CSV = its rounding)
recommended.openfoam: atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity / atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon with Uref, Zref, z0 and d = 0; nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 on the ground: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds them

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: U_H, the approach speed at the cube height (the tunnel's units)

theta.meaning: T_floor = 45.01 degC, T_floor - T_H = 30.26 K (the workbook's values at full precision)

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: uv run python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (pyproject.toml)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: RS_caseL.csv's temperature column is headed 'T(K)' but holds DEGREES CELSIUS (12.85 .. 29.86); AF_caseL.csv's 'T(K)' is kelvin (283 .. 295). The API serves degrees Celsius for both.

The published CSV is the workbook rounded to 2-4 decimals; the table is rebuilt from the workbook. Its 'tc' column (temperature-concentration covariance, K ppm) and the workbook's 'Usc' (the vector magnitude of the mean velocity) are not in the table.
BD_caseL.stl: the two bottom triangles (z = 0) of each of the 126 cubes (252 triangles) are wound inward; the served geometry.stl is the 126 boxes, outward.
The readme's file list names AF_caseK.csv and RS_caseK.csv; the files are AF_caseL.csv and RS_caseL.csv.
The readme's 'building surface temperature T_b = 14.8 degC' is the approach-flow air temperature at z = H; the workbook gives the building surface as 42.2 degC.
The line source is 0.037 m x 1.2 m in the readme and data paper but a 0.04 m x 1.02 m patch in BD_caseL.stl.

The +y and -y halves are not mirror images: the same point differs in U by 26 %, in k by 23 %, in C by 36 % on average, and U is 0.11 m/s lower and T 1.3 K higher at +y at z = 0.15 m (0.09 m above the roofs), so the tunnel flow has a lateral gradient; do not assume symmetry.
The workbook carries no expanded uncertainty (the data paper mentions one for Case J only).
AF_caseL.csv lists the profile from the top (z = 0.32 m) down and has no k.

The measured tracer flux through the cross-sections equals q / 1.2 m to 0.86 .. 1.0 (street and cube-column lines averaged), which fixes q and the unit ppm; the cube-column line alone carries only 0.2 .. 0.4 of it.
